review_description: Louis from Austra Solar Energy provide a very good service to our solar panels installation.The workmanship is excellent, price is compatiable.
Very helpful and efficient in all aspects from quote to install

One of the reasons we didnâ€™t choose another company is because they wouldnâ€™t come out to quote. Also they were very negative, in writing, about their competitors.Another sent a very young and seemingly inexperienced representative who had to go back to higher authorities for answers.The last are not based around here.

We were extremely impressed with Stephen's knowledge of his products and trusted his recommendations re brands, sizes, etc. They aligned, for the most part, with the recommendations of this site. Stephen was very prompt with the process, was one of the few installers we contacted who visited us to check out our circumstances (beyond the Google earth  photo) when working out a quote and answered any queries we had patiently, clearly and appropriately. We felt comfortable with his guidance. The installation process was quick (within a week), the testing by Powercor within a few days and connection to the meter took only a day after the application had been submitted. The electrician, Ryan, who was in charge of the installation was very patient while answering our many questions and they worked quickly and efficiently.They included in their quote the cost of a 10 - year - factory warranty on the Goodwe converter which convinced us to choose this brand rather than the more expensive Fronius brand.  It's interesting to be able to review how much power we are producing from our internet devices. So far we have had no issues, even though it is early days yet.  We are yet to get our first power bill and work out the best FIT.  We would recommend the reliability and professionalism of this branch of Solar Australia to install your solar system.PS We contacted 7 installers in total - only 3 visited us directly and two of those were not as familiar with their products as Solar Australia. Also, at least two of them criticised their competitors which we considered very unprofessional.
We have had to get the transformer capability checked by SP Ausnet so are still waiting on them until the system can be fitted.
All went well, company was exceptional to deal with and thanks so much Finn for your help

Had a number of issues with salesman not being honest with me. A main reason for going with Solar Australia was that I was promised it would be done before Christmas. He said the 20th December. I contacted them on the 19th and was told there was a problem getting Fronius inverter. So would be in the new year. If this was an issue then I should not have had to contact Solar Australia to find there was an issue. This did not suit as I was going to India in the new year then back to work. I sent an email asking for my deposit to be returned.I was contacted by the manager within minutes who said he knew nothing about me wanting it done before Christmas even though it was clearly communicated to the salesman. He said my panels AND Fronius inverter was in stock and scheduled for 8 January. This did not suit as I was in India. Someone was not being honest.He made special arrangements for the system to be installed on 28 December. I had arranged for a 5.3kw system using Trina panels. He said I could have a 6kw Talesun system for the same price and in his opinion were better than the Trina panels. I chose the 6kw system even though Talesun was not on your list.It all seems to be working well.The process did cause a bit of stress which I wanted to avoid by going through Solar Quotes.
Customer service so far has been excellent. Looking forward to having the system installed and to generating my own power!
They installed exactly what they said they would also on the day they arranged all my questions were answered promptly. A good company to.deal with.

The process, with recommended company, was a very easy process. We. Chose a company that we could have follow up service with and used reputable installers employed by themselves, not subcontracted. I have rated good as I believe fantastic requires a service that could not be improved on, and even though the service was very high quality, we have nothing else to gauge by. We thank Solar Australia for a great service.
Took about 10 weeks from sign up day to installation day but system is up and running now.

The quality of the solar components seem to be very good. I first contacted Solar Australia early December 2017 and the process of installation and follow up service has just been completed. The quality of the installation was in my opinion quite poor and had to get the installer back to rectify some of the problems. The final outcome was below my expectations. I had another Electrician look at the install and he was of a similar opinion to mine. I would not recommend this installer to my friends.

The inverter causes major interference to radio communications which is against the law as under the "Radiocommunications Act" Commonwealth. I expect at anytime to be instructed to close it down by Commonwealth inspectors but the installer and Goodwee although having full knowledge of this have done nothing to correct the situation.For converting the suns power to electricity and saving me money on the purchase of electricity it is very very good. Actual energy purchased on one bill was $15 and the second bill was $35 whereas I have saved hundreds of dollars on each. The battery capacity of 7.5kw of course helps but this also causes the radio communications interference via the inverter. This may cost a lot if I'm told by the Commonwealth to switch the whole system off. Solar Australia have offered at my cost and at my risk a filter system that may or may not work. As the quoted cost is not minor I feel that I have not been properly supported by this company.During installation for some reason the front half of my house was separated from the rest and this low load section accounts for most of my purchased energy burn each day. The heavy use system is supplied by the solar direct or via the batteries which on a normal day have some energy more than the 16% needed retention left.

Have had 2 electricity bills since the system went in.So far all we can say is: Money well spent.1. Bill: $284.52 Solar: $151.95 CR = $131.42 for 18 Oct 17 - 12 Jan 18 (change of plan etc etc)2. Bill: $377.80 Solar: $328.65 CR = $49.15 for 3 months!

Great salesperson and installation.Did research into Solar Australia, first to respond to inquiry, been in business a lot longer than most others, local office and people, viewed warehouse and offices, checked reviews, salesman knowledgeable and not pushy great advice and helpful..... installed system everything good to go pending meter changeover...... a week later checked with my energy supplier as to progress of meter application. No record of application. Called Solar Australia no answer, called following day no answer (getting nervous) called following day no answer (crap) called electrical sub contractor who advised Solar Australia had gone out of business.  Checked ASIC and sure enough two days after install, company listed ASIC website as in liquidation. Dealt with Energy Australia who were great assisting me to lodge application for meter change.Very sour taste in our mouth, considering I thought I had done all I could to ensure this didn't turn out this way. Don't know what else I could have done, now trying to get some sort of recognition from Enphase and Taelsun re warranty install date....not holding my breath....all I have in receipt is my bank records to show I have paid $9275 to Solar Australia....hope some of their creditors don't come knocking wanting their goods back.....

Out of the 3 quotes Solar Aus actually quoted on the inverter and features I wanted instead of trying to push me to other inferior inverters (that they were probably trying to shift from old stock).Although there was a 2 month delay on the Fronius due to lack of supply, the eventual install went very well.  We had 13.8kW installed on the shed with a 12.5kW inverter, the inverter was installed inside the shed in the location where I requested, and the system has been performing well.  The team of 3-4 guys had the numerous panels installed neatly by late morning/early afternoon with no shortcuts taken.Had some initial issues over the following weeks with the system cutting out due to high grid voltage, the technician returned at no charge to adjust some tolerances on the inverter which have mostly fixed the issue.  Ausgrid are attending next week to re-tap the pole transformer serving our farm, which should fix it for good.I'd highly recommend the team, very thorough, including the detailed information booklet handed over at the end of the job with expected solar outputs each month, circuit diagrams, system designs etc which I've never had on any of my other 4 solar systems in the past.

On the 27th October, we had a 6kw(20 x 300w panels) system, 5kw Goodwe hybrid inverter, and 10kw BYD BBox battery storage system installed. With the exception of the battery system being delivered the previous day, the installation was completed most efficiently and professionally in one day: no fuss, no mess, no broken tiles, and clear explanations and instructions.We were especially happy!I would have rated all the above categories as "Fantastic" if it hadn't been for the Goodwe inverter: the yellow Wi-fi  LED, unpredictably, went from solid to blinking 4 times which indicated a server problem. I tried several times to have the matter fixed or solved. Eventually, several days ago, I received a phone call from a Solar Australia engineer who, after listening to my narrative of what was happening, explained very clearly why the wi-fi LED was blinking, and reassured me that our system is functioning well, and that there is nothing to worry about. As I understand it, the number of inverters trying to communicate with the Goodwe portal during the day has caused the problem which Goodwe is presently working on. The glitch has no effect on the recording or presentation of data to the apps related to the system; it certainly has no effect on our energy distribution; all our needs are being met without using energy from the grid, and we are supplying energy to the grid.I would advise any consumer with a similar problem to demand a conversation with one of the company's engineers.All this being said, I highly recommend Solar Australia; they are highly professional and their products appear to be sound quality. We are very happy that we contracted them to install our solar system.

This was an additional solar system to our residence .. i.e. Had a 1.5k for several years facing east - now added a 2.2k facing North a total of 3.7k & it all seems to be working fine.. still have to receive our first "Net" account from AGL.In conjunction they removed our controlled load meter & tone control Hot water boost equipment - as we have a solar HWS that we have a switch in side the residence to switch the boost element on/off when required.. a saving of the fee for this as it is rarely used & can now select when needed considering that we are on "Time of use" metering" - cheaper after 10pm - 7am & weekends/public holidays..I just wish that a system could be devised to allow people could to "go off grid" using local power in the advent of a major interruption to the grid during daylight hours - keeping essential items going - a lot of power going to waste around Australia when blackouts occur could be eliminated, i realise that safety & synchronising is the issue - but feel this could be resolved!

The two other quotes were cheap but that was for a reason. We have a metal roof with a low incline and have had problems with leakage in the past when skylights were installed. SolarAustralia recommended a system that meant the panels would not be attached directly to the roof to avoid leakage problems. The other suppliers who only dealt with me on the phone and made their quotes based on Google Earth picture of our roof - never discussed how to avoid leakage problems.  One of the quotes put all the responsibility of the suitability of our roof on our shoulders if we went ahead - even though I feel this should be more their expertise than mine. One supplier recommended that we get an inverter for each panel - an increased cost of $3000 - on the basis if the roof was partly shaded - with only one inverter for the whole system - the system would not work at all.  I found out that this was not true. Solar Australia by getting up on our roof also recommended that we have some panels facing the east to catch the first sun in the morning when I would be washing etc.

I obtained three quotes. None were recommended by Solar Quotes only because none of the latter were found in my area.  My experience with potential suppliers was highly variable. One supplier I only spoke to on the phone and he put a lot of pressure on me to sign up immediately with a 10% deposit.  When I declined I was contacted several times with an offer and price that "expired today".  "Today" was extended however when he kept calling back.  This was the cheapest quote by far but I declined it.  I had to press for the name of the supplied panels and inverter and my own research suggested they were not the best quality. A second quote on the phone was more professional but on investigation of the hardware, I was convinced it would not suit me. Also, advice over the phone about my ability to export to the grid was ambiguous and, as I subsequently found out, not really correct. This was the middle of the three quotes. The company I went with sent a rep to look over my rural NSW property and was careful to explain potential difficulties in exporting power back to the grid. There was no pressure to sign up immediately and payment in full only came after completion. ie they required no deposit. They provided top quality panels and inverter and I can easily upgrade to battery storage in the future if I so choose. This provider charged the most but I am convinced it was the best option. In my experience I learned three things. Firstly, cheapest is not best. Secondly, do not be pressured into signing over the phone. Thirdly,  insist on knowing precisely what brands they are providing to you and do your own homework.
